title: Console walkthrough: usage analytics & cost breakdown - Silverline Retail
summary: Redwood AE and SE walked Silverline through the Console usage analytics, per-route dashboards and a sample cost breakdown. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for retail personalization; main concerns are cost, latency, and SOC2 / VPC requirements. Agreed next steps: send detailed pricing sheet, security pack (SOC2 + network diagrams), and schedule pilot/benchmarks with sample traffic.
next_steps: Maya to send pricing sheet and sample contract - by 2026-04-07
Diego to share benchmark checklist and SSE guide - by 2026-04-09
Jordan to provide sample route list and 1 week traffic profile - by 2026-04-10
Schedule pilot kickoff meeting - target week of 2026-04-20
action_items: Maya: attach pricing and Dedicated config options (due 2026-04-07)
Diego: prepare end-to-end benchmark plan + data mask checklist (due 2026-04-09)
Jordan: upload sample prompt set & traffic profile to shared drive (due 2026-04-10)
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're gonna do a quick Console walkthrough - focus on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdowns. I'm Maya, AE on this account. Diego from SE will drive the demo.

[00:15] Jordan Lee: Hi all, Jordan here. Excited to see how you break down the cost per route, that's our big ask.

[00:30] Diego Ramos: Cool. Quick agenda: Console home -> usage analytics -> route dashboards -> cost breakdown examples -> Q&A and next steps. I'll jump in. Please shout if you want us to pause.

[00:58] Diego Ramos: (screen share) This is the Redwood Consol dashboard, home page. You'll see high level token usage, error rates, and latency percentiles. Note the time selector up here, you can drill to 1h/24h/7d or custom.

[01:20] Priya Patel: Are those charts real-time? we have spikes during peak commerce hours.

[01:30] Diego Ramos: They're near-real time, ~20-30s lag depending on ingestion backpressure. For Dedicated customers we offer lower ingestion latency with longer retention as part of the premium observability pack.

[02:05] Diego Ramos: Now usage analytics - you can break down usage by model, by route, by API key, or by user/team. Here I'm filtering to route: /personalization/recommend and last 7 days.

[02:30] Marco Diaz: When you say route, is that a per-endpoint config or per-API-key?

[02:40] Diego Ramos: Both. Routes are logical config names in the Console - you can map them to API keys, services, or hostnames. So cost attribution can be by route or API key depending on what you need.

[03:05] Diego Ramos: Here's the per-route dashboard. It shows tokens in, tokens out, average latency p50/p95/p99, and cost estimate. The cost estimate uses your configured model mixes and quantization profiles.

[03:30] Jordan Lee: How accurate is the cost estimate? we need something close to chargeback for our finance team.

[03:45] Diego Ramos: Good question. The Console uses the same underlying billing engine as our API. For hosted it's very close to actual charge - within 2-5% historically. For Dedicated or private you'll upload your committed price per GPU-hour and the Console will translate that into per-token unit costs based on empirical throughput. There's a modeling step but we can generate a reconciliation report.

[04:20] Diego Ramos: Also note the route-level breakdown shows model fallbacks - if you set a fallback to a smaller model on high-latency thresholds, you'll see that reflected in the cost curve.

[04:45] Priya Patel: Can we set automatic fallbacks per route? we want to degrade to cheaper models during peak spikes.

[04:55] Diego Ramos: Yes, the routing policy allows priority lists and latency/cost SLO triggers. You can choose 'latency-first', 'cost-first', or custom rules. We also provide simulated rollouts in the Sandbox.

[05:30] (crosstalk) Jordan Lee: Sorry, quick pause - security: if we go Dedicated in our VPC, is usage telemetry still visible in Redwood Console?

[05:45] Maya Chen: Telemetry visibility is configurable. For Private deployments you can self-host the Console or opt into a proxy that surfaces anonymized metrics. For Dedicated we store aggregated metrics in the Redwood control plane - but we can provide retention controls and SOC2 logs.

[06:10] Marco Diaz: We need SOC2 evidence, SSO/SAML integration, and KMS support for keys.

[06:20] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We'll share the security pack after this call - SOC2 Type II attestation, network diagrams for VPC peering, SAML/SCIM support, and KMS/HSM options.

[06:45] Diego Ramos: Moving on - here's an example cost breakdown. We took three top routes and projected monthly cost given current traffic. Route A (/search) is chatty but short responses - high requests, moderate tokens. Route B (/recommend) has larger context windows, so token cost dominates. Route C (/nlp/bulk) is embeddings/agg.

[07:20] Diego Ramos: For each route you can toggle model variants and quantization level - see how cost changes immediately. For example switching a route from base-7B to quantized-4bit runtime drops unit token cost ~40% in this model profile.

[07:50] Jordan Lee: Do you have automated suggestions? we don't want to manually tune 30 routes.

[08:00] Diego Ramos: That's where Redwood Optimize recommendations live. Console will suggest batching, cacheable prefixes, and model/quantization swaps per route. Recommendations include estimated savings and expected latency changes. We can export a tuning plan.

[08:25] Priya Patel: How do you estimate savings for batching? our traffic pattern has many small requests so batching is appealing but may add latency.

[08:40] Diego Ramos: The estimator uses your traffic histogram to propose batch windows. You can set a latency SLO per route and the optimizer computes the largest batch that meets p95/p99 constraints. We also show cache hit rate projections if you enable prefix/KV caching.

[09:10] Diego Ramos: Here's the per-token cost table - tokens in, tokens out, unit price. Note we separate model compute cost and infra/overhead. For Dedicated customers we let you override infra cost based on committed GPUs.

[09:40] Marco Diaz: For Dedicated, how granular is the billing? we need per-biz-unit showback.

[09:55] Maya Chen: You can map routes to business units and export CSVs or push to your billing system via our Billing API. There's also webhook support for daily usage snapshots.

[10:20] Diego Ramos: Quick demo of route-level anomalies: Console flags sudden latency regressions and correlates with deployment events and model rollouts, so you can see if a newer model caused the spike.
transcript_continued:
[10:50] Jordan Lee: Nice. Can the Console tie into our internal tracing? we use OpenTelemetry.

[11:05] Diego Ramos: Yes, we ingest OpenTelemetry spans - there's a connector. We can also add trace IDs in the response metadata so your logs can correlate requests end-to-end.

[11:35] Priya Patel: About retention, how long is detailed token-level data kept? Compliance needs at least 12 months of audit logs.

[11:50] Maya Chen: By default hosted keeps 90 days for raw per-request payloads and 2 years for aggregated metrics. For enterprise we offer extended retention and export hooks to S3 or your data lake. For Private deployments you control retention.

[12:20] Diego Ramos: Back to cost breakdown - here's a sample scenario: if we enable a 150ms batch window and quantized runtime for the recommendation route, cost drops 28% while p95 latency increases by 30ms, still within your 300ms SLO.

[12:55] Jordan Lee: Hmm, our commerce page target for recommend is 250ms p95. 300ms might be too high.

[13:05] Diego Ramos: Understood - optimizer can restrict proposals that push above your SLO. Another option is Dedicated capacity where throughput improves, lowering p95 while keeping batching benefits.

[13:30] Marco Diaz: Can Dedicated run mixed model sizes across nodes? we'd like a hot pool for p50/p95 sensitive routes and a cold pool for cheaper inference.

[13:45] Diego Ramos: Yes, Dedicated supports pool tagging and routing policies. Smart routing can steer requests to hot instances based on route tags or latency budgets.

[14:05] Priya Patel: About data residency - some of our users are EU-based and we need logs and data in eu-west only.

[14:20] Maya Chen: We have region-aware routing and data residency controls. For hosted EU regions we can keep control plane telemetry in-region, and for strict needs Private deployment in your VPC is an option.

[14:50] Diego Ramos: I'm going to open the Sandbox route simulator. We can simulate 10k RPS with your sample histogram and show cost/latency tradeoffs.

[15:10] Jordan Lee: That would be great. We'll need a checklist of what to provide: routes, sample input payloads, expected traffic distribution.

[15:30] Diego Ramos: I'll send a benchmark checklist - includes sample payloads, auth tokens, expected concurrency, and a list of routes. Also data masking guidance.

[15:55] Diego Ramos: Quick note on quantization: not all model families degrade the same. We have verified profiles for the common open models and some proprietary families; quantization-friendly models keep quality within a small delta.

[16:20] Jordan Lee: Where can we see the evaluation scores? we want to validate quality after quantization.

[16:30] Diego Ramos: Console links to Evals - you can run your golden prompts and get output diffs. We can hook the evals to route-level regression alerts.

[16:55] Priya Patel: On the topic of fallbacks: if fallback triggers mid-request, do you support streaming partial responses? concerns about UX if response stops.

[17:10] Diego Ramos: We have graceful degradation policies: streaming continues and a model switch can be performed on new tokens, but we recommend idempotent or chunked UX patterns. It's an engineering tradeoff.

[17:35] Marco Diaz: Procurement question - are there minimum commitments for Dedicated?

[17:45] Maya Chen: Typically a 3-6 month reserved capacity minimum for Dedicated. We can discuss flexible bursts during the pilot.

[18:00] Jordan Lee: Cost-wise, do you provide predictive monthly estimates if traffic grows 2x?

[18:10] Diego Ramos: Yes, the Console has a "what-if" planner. You can scale traffic and toggle model configs to see projected monthly bill and per-route showback.

[18:30] Diego Ramos: I'm going to open a CSV export example - you can export per-route daily aggregates and ingest into your finance tools.

[18:50] Priya Patel: Do you have API endpoints for pulling usage programmatically? we want to automate internal chargeback.

[18:58] Diego Ramos: Yep, REST Billing API, token-limited. We also have webhooks and S3 exports.

[19:20] Jordan Lee: Any gotchas for embeddings routes? we use them heavily for semantic search.

[19:35] Diego Ramos: Embeddings are charged slightly differently - unit is per-embedding vector and storage. Console shows vector compute vs storage cost. Also note caching works differently; you can cache vectors to reduce repeated compute.

[20:00] Marco Diaz: For pilot, we need an NDA and a statement on data handling.

[20:10] Maya Chen: We'll attach the NDA with the pricing packet. The security pack has data handling details.

[20:30] Diego Ramos: Quick walkthrough of anomaly detection - Console flagged a regresson last week where a model rollout increased tokens per request by ~15% because of system prompts. You can set auto-rollback rules.

[20:55] Jordan Lee: Auto-rollback is big for us. reduce blast radius.

[21:05] Diego Ramos: We support canary and A/B rollouts and automatic fallbacks to previous model if certain KPI thresholds exceed.

[21:25] Priya Patel: Final question: is there SDK support for our Java stack?

[21:35] Maya Chen: We have official SDKs for Python, Node, and a community Java SDK. For enterprise customers we can prioritize a first-party Java client.

[21:55] Jordan Lee: Great. Thanks, this was helpful. Next steps recap?

[22:05] Maya Chen: Recap: we'll send pricing + NDA, security pack, benchmark checklist. Diego will run a sandbox sim when you provide traffic profile. Jordan to share routes and sample inputs. We'll aim to kick off pilot week of 2026-04-20.

[22:30] Marco Diaz: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.

[22:45] (meeting ends)
